title: Human Reproduction
seo_title: Grade 12 Life Sciences: Human Reproduction Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_text: The structure of the male and female reproductive systems; puberty and the role of hormones; gametogenesis (spermatogenesis and oogenesis); the menstrual cycle and its hormonal control (FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone); fertilisation, implantation and the development of the zygote; the placenta and the role of the amnion and umbilical cord. (summary of CAPS Life Sciences, Grade 12, Life Sciences: Human reproduction)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Life Sciences worksheets (CAPS): the reproductive systems, puberty, gametogenesis, the menstrual cycle, fertilisation, implantation and the placenta. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: FSH and LH from the pituitary control the menstrual cycle.
key_sub: Fertilisation happens in the Fallopian tube.
body_html:
How to think about it

Sperm are made in the testes by meiosis (spermatogenesis) under the control of testosterone. Eggs develop in follicles in the ovaries (oogenesis). Puberty starts when the pituitary gland releases FSH and LH.

In the menstrual cycle, FSH makes a follicle grow, which releases oestrogen; a surge of LH causes ovulation on about day 14; the corpus luteum releases progesterone, which keeps the uterus lining thick. If the egg is fertilised in the Fallopian tube, the zygote divides and implants in the endometrium; the placenta passes food and oxygen to the foetus through the umbilical cord.

Example

Which hormone causes ovulation?

A surge mid-cycle

Answer: LH

Example

Where is the zygote implanted?

The thick lining

Answer: in the endometrium of the uterus

Common mistakes

  • Thinking ovulation and menstruation are the same.
  • Thinking the mother's blood flows into the foetus.
  • Mixing up FSH and LH.

faq.q: Why does the uterus lining break down if no pregnancy happens?
faq.a: The corpus luteum degenerates, so the progesterone level falls.
It holds amniotic fluid that protects the foetus from shocks and drying out.
